bio: If you're looking for a steakhouse in the Palermo area, just a few steps from the Carlos Thays Botanical Garden, this is a great option. The restaurant, which catches the eye thanks to its display window featuring cuts of meat being slow roasted in front of your eyes, features a long bar with stools facing the coals (fueled by firewood, to add a subtle smoky flavour) and a dining area that seats about 30 guests. Between these two areas is a dry-ageing room, where you can see large cuts of beef being dry-aged. The à la carte, though not very extensive, features interesting appetisers, such as beef tongue with vinaigrette or the delicious chicken pâté with pickled turnips and a Port wine reduction, as well as some incredibly flavourful grilled main courses (900 g bone-in ribeye, 900 g Milanese cutlet, grilled ribs, etc.), prepared in the traditional rural style but with an innovative twist. For dessert, don't miss the flan—it's incredibly creamy!
